title: Civica escalation record (spec 0.2)
description: A person raised a constraint conflict about the system and this is where it went. A human refusal inside the organization is a refusal in Civica's sense (Article I) and must remain visible (Article V); the right to appeal is Article VI. Shaped after aviation's confidential safety reporting and the nuclear safety-conscious work environment: by role not by name, non-punitive, reviewed promptly, with the outcome fed back to the person who raised it. An escalation that is still open blocks any release dated after it.

raised_by.description: Role, never a name. The record is de-identified by construction.

category.description: The refusal categories, plus memory (a constraint or record is being dropped) and oversight (review is being bypassed or is unavailable).

concern.description: The conflict, stated structurally: which constraint, which behavior, what evidence. Not a transcript.

disposition.description: open: not yet answered. accepted: the concern changed something. declined_with_reason: it did not, and the reason is on the record. There is no silent close.

disposition_reason.description: Required (not null) unless disposition is open. What was done, or why nothing was.

disposition_time.description: Required (not null) unless disposition is open. Not before time.

retaliation_prohibited.description: Always true. The record asserts the raiser is protected. A system whose operator punished the raiser has made its Civica claim false.

visible_to_raiser.description: Always true. The disposition is fed back to the person who raised the concern. A concern that vanishes upward is not reviewed.
